instruction:
You are interviewing a shop about a job they already do, until the procedure is unambiguous enough that two different technicians working alone would produce the same record. Ask about ONE thing per turn, in their language, never in the vocabulary of forms. Compile only when nothing material is still unstated: every step has a reason someone would accept, every field has an acceptance rule that can actually be applied to what comes back, and a bound that came from the shop rather than from you. Inventing a tolerance is the one thing you must never do — a figure nobody stated must not appear in what you compile. A shop that does not know one will not know it when asked again: take the first 'I don't know' as final, keep it in unresolved if it matters, and move on. Your turns are few. Spend them on the figures that decide whether the job passed, never on detail beneath them.

Return JSON with these fields:
- mode (one of ask | compile, required): ask while anything material is unstated. compile once the procedure would run unambiguously.
- question (string, null when it does not apply): Required when mode is ask. One question about one thing, phrased for a mechanic, not a form designer. Never a list, never a preamble, never a restatement of what they just told you, and never one they have already said they cannot answer.
- asks_about (one of scope | sequence | tolerance | evidence | failure | authority | parts | safety, null when it does not apply): Which class of unknown this question closes. Required when mode is ask.
- unresolved (array, required): Everything you still do not know that would change the compiled procedure. Complete every turn, not only what you just asked about. Empty is the only condition under which you may compile.
- understanding (string, required): What you now believe the job is, in two sentences. Written every turn so the shop can correct you early rather than at the end.
- draft (object, null when it does not apply): Required when mode is compile. The procedure as it would run tomorrow.

output.understanding: The job is a pre-ride inspection and inflation of both tyres on a Segway Xyber e-bike to prevent dangerous failures in traffic. The rider inspects the tyres for damage, pumps them to the maximum pressure printed on the sidewall, and signs off before riding.

draft.title: Pre-Ride Tyre Inspection and Inflation
disqualifiers: Cracks or sidewall splits found on either tyre
Cuts or thorns in the tread that feel too deep
releases: Safe to ride in traffic and on gravel

steps.title: Visual Inspection
steps.explanation: Checking for glass, thorns, cracks, or splits prevents a tyre from letting go at speed in traffic.

fields.prompt: Are the tyres free of cracks and sidewall splits?
choices: Yes, tyres are free of cracks and splits
No, cracks or sidewall splits detected
fields.acceptance_target: Yes, tyres are free of cracks and splits
fields.guidance: Inspect both front and rear tyres closely. Any visible cracking or split in the sidewall means the tyre must be replaced.

fields.prompt: Are there any cuts or thorns in the tread that feel too deep?
choices: Yes, cuts or thorns feel too deep
fields.guidance: Feel any cuts or thorns in the tread to judge if they have penetrated too deep. If they feel unsafe, the tyre must be replaced.

steps.title: Front Tyre Inflation
steps.explanation: Inflating the front tyre to its specific maximum pressure ensures optimal grip and prevents pinch flats or blowouts.

fields.prompt: Take a photo of the front tyre sidewall showing the max pressure rating.
fields.acceptance_description: The maximum PSI or Bar rating printed on the front tyre sidewall.
fields.guidance: Locate and photograph the maximum pressure specification moulded onto the side of the front tyre.

fields.prompt: Take a photo of the pump gauge showing the final front tyre pressure.
fields.guidance: Pump the tyre until the gauge matches the limit shown on the sidewall, then photograph the gauge clearly.

steps.title: Rear Tyre Inflation
steps.explanation: Inflating the rear tyre to its specific maximum pressure ensures it can handle the rider's weight and power without failing.

fields.prompt: Take a photo of the rear tyre sidewall showing the max pressure rating.
fields.acceptance_description: The maximum PSI or Bar rating printed on the rear tyre sidewall.
fields.guidance: Locate and photograph the maximum pressure specification moulded onto the side of the rear tyre.

fields.prompt: Take a photo of the pump gauge showing the final rear tyre pressure.
fields.guidance: Pump the tyre until the gauge matches the limit shown on the sidewall, then photograph the gauge clearly.

steps.title: Rider Sign-Off
steps.explanation: A personal sign-off ensures the rider takes responsibility for confirming the bike is safe before entering traffic.

fields.prompt: Sign to clear the bike for the road.
fields.guidance: Your signature confirms that both tyres have been inspected, inflated to spec, and are safe to ride.
